today.name: Databench by Alkera
today.tagline: Open-source collaborative agentic workspace for data teams
today.description: Databench by Alkera is the open-source, multiplayer workspace for data science, analytics, and engineering. Collaborate live alongside teammates and agents in notebooks and chats, run any cell or agent on your laptop, another computer, or a GPU node and launch many agents in parallel to explore ideas. Every result traces back to the data and code behind it. Try it at https://alkera.ai with a generous free tier or host Databench yourself (https://github.com/AlkeraAI/Databench).

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! 👋 I'm Rick, co-founder of Alkera, building Databench with Andrew Tran and Tony Li. Before starting Alkera, we worked closely with data teams at places including TikTok, Ramp, and Hudson River Trading.Alkera provides a unified platform for data engineering, data science, and data analytics work. We've noticed a significant need for an agent-native data science solution beyond traditional Jupyter notebooks.❌ The ProblemWhile new agent-native interfaces such as ADEs have significantly increased software engineers' productivity, data teams are still stuck with the traditional Jupyter notebook, with little evolution or adaptation for agent-first, collaborative workflows. Another problem with agentic work for data is the lack of accountability, traceability, and reproducibility, which makes it hard to verify and reproduce agent-generated work.This is why we built Databench, the open-source multiplayer workspace for data science, analytics, and engineering. Work alongside teammates and agents in notebooks and chats and run any cell or agent on your laptop or a remote computing node.✅ What Databench provides:Open-source subset of the Alkera product licensed under Apache 2.0Multiplayer SQL and Python notebooks that you share live with teammates and agentsConnection to databases that are SQLAlchemy compatible (PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL, and many more)Reactive notebooks based on marimo that rerun stale cells based on changes to SQL & PythonFully web-based with rich file editors and notebook editingLive collaboration with live cursors and edits from teammates and agentsRun chats and notebooks anywhere: your laptop, a remote compute node, or a GPU clusterDeclarative charting library for pretty graphs every time in your notebooksTry it free at https://alkera.ai or self-host from GitHub: https://github.com/AlkeraAI/DatabenchIf you have any questions or concerns, the team will be online all day to help!

today.name: Pegasus 1.6 by TwelveLabs
today.tagline: Transforms egocentric video into robot training data
today.description: Pegasus 1.6 is the TwelveLabs model that understands video from a first-person point of view, built for the egocentric and teleoperated footage robotics and physical AI teams already collect. It recognizes entities more accurately, and produces persistent metadata across segment types. Point it at raw teleoperation or wearable footage and get back labeled, timestamped, robot-ready data. No manual labeling pass required.

comments.text: Hi everyone, I'm Aiden, co-founder and CTO at TwelveLabs. Excited to share Pegasus 1.6 with you today.Every robotics and physical AI team we talk to is sitting on the same problem: hours of first-person footage that's the raw material for action labeling and next-action prediction, and no foundation model actually built to understand it. General-purpose video models are trained on broadcast and third-person footage. Point them at a wearable or a robot's own camera and they miss what's actually happening.Pegasus 1.6 is our answer. It's the first TwelveLabs model built for egocentric (first-person) video understanding. Pegasus 1.6 expands on Pegasus 1.5's Time-Based Metadata (TBM), which extracts timestamped, structured metadata from custom schemas, by adding support for egocentric video and task narration. We've also sharpened detailed recognition of hand, tool, and object interactions , while speeding up processing for high-volume video workloads. As an update to 1.5’s capabilities, we also have improved performance on in-depth metadata extraction and on grounded entity recognition, the ability to name a character based on context clues in the video. Concretely, for robotics and data teams that means: point Pegasus at raw egocentric clips and get back structured action labels, compliance ratings, and timestamps you can use directly in a training pipeline instead of a manual labeling pass that costs $4–$22/hour of footage.Physical AI is a new domain for us, so if you're working with egocentric (human or teleoperated) data and hit edge cases, I want to hear about them. Thanks!

today.name: Mistral Large 4

today.description: Mistral Large 4 (aka Le Chonk) is Mistral's largest model yet: a natively multimodal mixture of experts model with 1T total and 49B active parameters and a 1M token context window. It's a browser with your Claude Code or Codex working alongside you. When something on a page gives you an idea, you say so right there, and an agent starts on it in the right project. You don't have to spend time looking for the right folder, rephrasing everything you just saw on the web, and you don't switch in and out of work mode. The work goes on with you in the flow.This matters now more than ever. Agents have shortened the distance between ideas to output near zero. So the bottleneck is capturing the idea at the moment you have it. That moment is nearly always while you're taking something in, and that is what a browser is for.Rill is a free AI-native browser. yesterday.name: AUDR by Chargebee
yesterday.tagline: Open standard for tracking agent run costs
yesterday.description: AUDR (Agent Usage Detail Record) is an open standard, for capturing who initiated an agent run and what it cost across every system that run touches. Inspired by the telecom industry's Call Detail Record, AUDR defines a common JSON schema that any harness, router, or billing system can emit and ingest. Three core rules make it work: a shared run ID minted by the harness, clear field ownership, and strict merge rules where conflicts are rejected and corrections are new records.

yesterday.name: Ghostifier

yesterday.description: Instead of one form per company, Ghostifier starts from your inbox. It finds who holds your data, unsubscribes you and opts you out of sale and sharing on day one, waits out the return window, then sends deletion requests and tracks every reply. Banks, insurers and your employer are left alone. It also asks data brokers to delete you. Gmail access is headers only, so it never reads your email bodies, and there is no AI: every decision follows fixed rules.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm Jonathan, and I built Ghostifier because I have a passion for technology and building tools, especially tools that work for me. I was overwhelmed with the constant inbox management, opting out of emails, unsubscribing, etc. but I knew those companies still stored my data. In an era of privacy and security, I wanted to go once step further. How it works: connect Gmail and it finds the companies that hold your data. Day one, it unsubscribes you and opts you out of sale and sharing. It then waits out the return window, so it doesn't cut off a refund, and only then sends a deletion request and tracks the reply. Banks, insurers, healthcare, schools, government and your employer are never sent one. What I think is different: It starts from your inbox, so you don't have to remember who has your data. You see what it will do before it does it, or switch on Autopilot. I build a one time scan / delete option as well as a continuous "always on" auto plan that will be your personal Ghosting Assistant. The scan is free; sending requests is on a paid plan. I'd love to hear which companies you'd want cleared first, and where the flow felt unclear.

there's a tension in the pitch that I'd want answered before connecting my real inbox: to find who holds your data you need fairly deep read access to the inbox itself, which means trusting one more company with everything already sitting in there to fix the problem of too many companies having your data. what's the actual scope of that access - does it need to read full message bodies to find these companies, or can it work off senders/headers alone? and is anything retained after the unsubscribe/deletion run finishes, or is it read-and-discard

I like the name, it's clever. I think many people are trying to figure out how to delete their digital footprint. This seems to go straight to the source, people's inbox. How does it compare to the big firms like Aura or Incogni?
Hello Ghostifier! I have a technical implementation question. How do you read only the Gmail email headers? Is this ability through the Gmail API?Congrats on today's launch!

Thank you for all of you that have signed up so far! It's so satisfying seeing something I built gain some traction!As I launch Ghostifier on ProductHunt, I'm trying to see how this type of product would land with you all. The Gmail Security Review process is lengthy and expensive, and before investing there, I want to validate with you all if this is a worth enough service to continue support. For those of you signing up and connecting Gmail, you may see a Google Warning during the authentication step, and that's normal! Hopefully we can improve that experience later on once we validate the product.And for you all that have been able to connect and scan, what was your experience like? Any weird bugs / behavior that wasn't clear or was confusing? I want to build Ghostifier to be as strong as it can be, and I need your help to do it!Thank you!

The “wait out the return window, then request deletion” workflow is a clever touch. I’m curious how Ghostifier determines that window and what happens when a company doesn’t respond or only partially fulfills a deletion request. Does the tracking continue until there’s a confirmed resolution?

week.name: Monospace from Directus

week.description: Monospace sits between enterprise data and everyone who builds on it. Connect any data source, and your developers, business teams, and AI agents get live, read-write access to it. comments.text: Hi Product Hunt... faComments.text: سلام به همه در Product Hunters! 👋 من لانگ، مدیرعامل اسپیرا AI هستم. سومین بار است در چند ماه اخیر اینجا راه‌اندازی می‌کنم و خوشحالم که دوباره برگشتم :) پس از دو راه‌اندازی قبلی من، مدام با یک دیوار یکسان برخورد می‌کردم: هوش مصنوعی می‌تواند یک کلیپ را در چند ثانیه تولید کند، اما تبدیل آن به چیزی که واقعاً منتشر کنید، هنوز به معنای باز کردن یک ویرایشگر است. انتخاب ارائه‌دهنده، برش ب‌رول، اصلاح زیرنویس‌ها و پیدا کردن موسیقی. تولید ارزان شده است. اما تمام کردن کار ارزان نشده است، و تمام کردن کار جایی است که همه به‌صورت خاموش تسلیم می‌شوند و محتوای بی‌کیفیت (slop) منتشر می‌کنند. به همین دلیل ما اسپیرا ماکسیما را آموزش دادیم: یک مدل ویدیوی اجتماعی که متن ساده را به یک ویدیوی UGC سبک وایرال و کامل تبدیل می‌کند که چیزی برای ویرایش باقی نمی‌ماند و فوراً آماده انتشار است. این‌طور کار می‌کند: اسکریپت خود را بچسبانید و آن یک ارائه‌دهنده مناسب با موضوع انتخاب می‌کند. ب‌رول و حرکت‌های ترند را در اطراف کلمات شما برش می‌زند، سپس زیرنویس و موسیقی اضافه می‌کند. می‌خواهید خودتان باشید؟ یک عکس و یک نمونه صدا کلون هوش مصنوعی شما را می‌سازند، با همان چهره و صدا در هر ویدیو. چیزی می‌فروشید؟ عکس‌های محصول را وارد کنید. قبلاً با تلفنتان فیلم گرفته‌اید؟ آن را آپلود کنید و آن ویرایش را حول محور شما می‌سازد. این مدل با داده‌های ترند و عملکرد اجتماعی آموزش پس‌دوره شده است، بنابراین ظاهر ویدیو با آنچه در فید این هفته جواب می‌دهد هم‌راستا است. ۵۰٪ تخفیف برای ماه راه‌اندازی، امیدواریم از آن لذت ببرید. بازخورد شما را دوست داریم: اگر یک مدل هر بار یک ویدیوی کامل به شما می‌داد، آیا هنوز می‌خواستید قبل از انتشار دستکاری کنید، یا اجازه می‌دادید ارسال شود؟ اسکریپتی که قرار بود منتشر کنید را بچسبانید و به من بگویید کجا عالی است و کجا ما را خجالت‌زده می‌کند. مشتاق شنیدن نظرات شما هستم!! 👇👇👇

week.name: Rill Browser
week.tagline: The browser where Claude Code and Codex work beside you
week.description: Rill is an AI-native browser built around the Claude Code and Codex you already use. Browse normally, then press ⌘E on any page to turn what you're looking at into a task for your agent. Rill finds the right project, passes along the context, and the agent works while you keep browsing. It also sorts your tabs into themes, turns your history into days you can search, and brings every project your agents are working on into one place. Free, on the plan you already have.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm William! I made Rill because I want to always stay in the flow. As an ADHD, I never liked code-switching. My best ideas for work come when I'm supposedly not working at all: watching something for fun, reading things and following a rabbit hole, looking at how someone else solved a problem. Then when an idea hit me, I'd have to stop, switch to coding agents, find the project and explain it all, and most of the time I just didn't.Rill is my way of removing that code-switching. It's a browser with your Claude Code or Codex working alongside you. When something on a page gives you an idea, you say so right there, and an agent starts on it in the right project. You don't have to spend time looking for the right folder, rephrasing everything you just saw on the web, and you don't switch in and out of work mode. The work goes on with you in the flow.This matters now more than ever. Agents have shortened the distance between ideas to output near zero. So the bottleneck is capturing the idea at the moment you have it. That moment is nearly always while you're taking something in, and that is what a browser is for.Rill is a free AI-native browser. It's WebKit-based, which means it's native to Mac. And it runs on the Claude Code or Codex plan you already have, so you don't have to buy a new subscription for all of its agentic capabilities.cHow do you keep an idea today when it shows up at the wrong time?

week.name: FastRouter.ai
week.tagline: Route requests to the right LLM for cost, latency & quality
week.description: FastRouter is a unified AI gateway and control plane for developers and enterprise teams building with LLMs. It routes every request to the right model across 200+ LLMs through one OpenAI-compatible API, optimizing for cost, latency, quality, and reliability. With intelligent routing, failover, observability, and governance, teams can scale AI apps without vendor lock-in or code changes.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! I’m RP, part of the team behind FastRouter.ai.We built FastRouter because running AI in production meant too much plumbing and too much guesswork: multiple SDKs, scattered dashboards, fragile failover, and no clear answer to “How do we make this cheaper without making it worse?” when all the logs are scattered all over the place.⚡ One integration. Less provider juggling.FastRouter gives you a unified API across major models and providers, with support for OpenAI, Anthropic Messages, and Gemini-compatible interfaces.Claude models, for example, are available through Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Vertex AI. FastRouter routes requests to healthy upstreams, so you don’t have to maintain separate SDK integrations and failover logic yourself.Routing is the starting point. Routing Intelligence is what makes FastRouter different.Most gateways show you traffic and spending. FastRouter helps you figure out what to change:Proactive cost insights: Weekly recommendations based on real traffic. Find cheaper models, prompt caching opportunities, and workloads suited to flex pricing. Model-switching recommendations include evals so you can compare quality before switching.Early warning signs: Spot latency drift, error spikes, and cost anomalies, with alerts delivered to Slack or PagerDuty.Request-level visibility: See which upstream served each request, allocate costs with tags, and inspect logs, including multimodal outputs.Evals beyond text: Evaluate production traffic and datasets, including images and video. A successful API response doesn’t always mean a usable output.Multimodal response caching: Reuse cached image and video responses for matching prompts or cache keys instead of calling the model again.Better prompt management: Keep prompts in a shared, versioned library, with optimization and compression tools to improve them.Our production customers are already saving $10K+ per month by acting on FastRouter’s recommendations.Available as SaaS or fully on-prem, with budget caps, alerts, and access controls built in.We built this to spend less time maintaining integrations and investigating bills, and more time shipping things that work.Claim 2 months free: https://fastrouter.ai/product-huntWhat’s your biggest AI production headache right now: reliability, cost, integrations, or quality? week.name: AUDR by Chargebee
week.tagline: Open standard for tracking agent run costs
week.description: AUDR (Agent Usage Detail Record) is an open standard, for capturing who initiated an agent run and what it cost across every system that run touches. Inspired by the telecom industry's Call Detail Record, AUDR defines a common JSON schema that any harness, router, or billing system can emit and ingest. Three core rules make it work: a shared run ID minted by the harness, clear field ownership, and strict merge rules where conflicts are rejected and corrections are new records.

Reads the situation you're writing into and adjusts how the text comes out. * Keeps your voice. Your slang, your shorthand, and your way of putting things stay. * Learns your words. Remembers the names and terms you correct, so you fix them once. * Translates as you speak. Say it in your language, send it in theirs. It reads native, not translated. * Ask AI. Say what you want written and it lands in the field. Ask a question and the answer opens in a window. It's free to try, and there's a free month of Pro during launch. Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.
